name: Estradiol
mechanism: Natural oestrogen (17β-estradiol) - binds to oestrogen receptors, reduces menopausal symptoms and bone resorption
dosing: HRT: Oral 1-2mg OD. Transdermal patch 25-100mcg twice weekly. Gel 0.5-1.5mg daily. Combine with progestogen if uterus present
contraindications: Oestrogen-dependent cancers (breast, endometrial), unexplained vaginal bleeding, active VTE/PE, untreated endometrial hyperplasia, active liver disease, acute porphyria
interactions: Enzyme inducers (↓ effect), warfarin (may ↑ or ↓ effect), corticosteroids (may ↑ effect)
monitoring: BP, breast examination, endometrial surveillance if uterus present. Review need annually. Mammography as per national screening
pregnancy: Contraindicated - not for use in pregnancy
sideEffects: Breast tenderness, nausea, leg cramps, headache, bloating, VTE risk (↑ with oral, lower with transdermal), stroke risk (small), breast cancer risk (with long-term use)
pharmacokinetics: Oral: variable absorption, extensive first-pass metabolism. Transdermal: avoids first-pass, steady levels. Half-life: 1 hour (oral), hepatic metabolism
clinicalPearls: Transdermal route preferred over oral (lower VTE risk, avoids first-pass). Always combine with progestogen if uterus present (prevents endometrial hyperplasia). Use lowest effective dose. Body-identical HRT increasingly preferred
indication: Menopausal symptoms (hot flushes, night sweats), osteoporosis prevention (not first-line), urogenital atrophy
